newsitem.title: UK: Shoe firm C & J Clark may sell two factory outlets.
newsitem.headline: Shoe firm C & J Clark may sell two factory outlets.

text.p: Shoe manufacturer C & J Clark Ltd, Britain's second largest private company, said on Wednesday it was considering options for two factory outlets, ranging from trade sale to a co-operative joint venture.

"The board, which has received expressions of interest from third parties, has decided that the operation may benefit from dedicated specialist management and separate ownership and funding," company chairman Roger Pedder said in a statement.
The company said it appointed Coopers and Lybrand Corporate Finance to assess the options for the two factory outlets at Street, Somerset in South Western England and Kendal in the North West.
Pedder said the consideration of options for the factory outlets was in line with company policy to redirect its core shoe operations.
The company said it operates seven factories in the UK and owns more than 600 shoe stores trading under the Clarks, "K" and Ravel names.
